agents.name: Claude Code
agents.verify: Run `/doctor prompt-audit` and look for the installed file in the audited list.
notes: Project and user memory load at session start; start a new session after installing.
`.claude/rules/` scopes rules to file types; `~/.claude/rules/` is the user-scope equivalent.
AGENTS.md is read in place of CLAUDE.md when no CLAUDE.md exists.

sources.quote: CLAUDE.md files: instructions you write to give Claude persistent context.
User instructions | ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md | Personal preferences for all projects

agents.name: Codex CLI

workspace.reason: Codex reads a global file and in-repository AGENTS.md files; an ancestor workspace file above the repository is not documented.

agents.verify: Ask Codex which instruction files it loaded; it builds the instruction chain once per run.
notes: Discovery follows a precedence order: global scope, then the repository root, then nested files closest to the code.
Codex reads AGENTS.override.md in preference to AGENTS.md at the same scope.
Code review rules go in a `## Code Review Rules` section of the AGENTS.md closest to the governed code.

sources.quote: Global scope: In your Codex home directory (defaults to ~/.codex, unless you set CODEX_HOME), Codex reads AGENTS.override.md if it exists.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot
agents.global_unsupported_reason: Copilot personal instructions are set in GitHub account settings, not a user-level file.

workspace.reason: Copilot reads AGENTS.md files anywhere within the repository; an ancestor workspace file above the repository is not documented.

agents.verify: Open the References list in the Copilot response to see which instruction files were used.
notes: When Copilot is working, the nearest AGENTS.md file in the directory tree takes precedence.
Repository-wide instructions live in a single .github/copilot-instructions.md file.

sources.quote: Repository-wide custom instructions apply to all requests made in the context of a repository. These are specified in a copilot-instructions.md file.
When Copilot is working, the nearest AGENTS.md file in the directory tree will take precedence.

agents.name: OpenCode

workspace.reason: opencode reads AGENTS.md from the project root and its subdirectories; an ancestor workspace file above the repository is not documented.

agents.verify: Ask opencode which instruction files it loaded for the session.
agents.local_models: Configure a local OpenAI-compatible provider in opencode.json.
notes: A project AGENTS.md applies only in that directory and its sub-directories.
The global file at ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md applies across all sessions.
`/init` creates or improves an existing AGENTS.md in place.

sources.quote: You can provide custom instructions to opencode by creating an AGENTS.md file.
You can also have global rules in a ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md file. This gets applied across all opencode sessions.

agents.name: Gemini CLI
agents.verify: Run `/memory reload` to re-scan and reload all GEMINI.md files; the CLI footer shows the number of loaded context files.
notes: The CLI loads GEMINI.md files from several locations and concatenates them, in order: global, environment and workspace, then just-in-time per directory.
The just-in-time scan reads a directory and its ancestors up to a trusted root.

sources.quote: The CLI searches for GEMINI.md files in your configured workspace directories and their parent directories.

agents.name: Aider
agents.global_unsupported_reason: Aider has no user-level instruction file; add the Doctrine file to `read:` in ~/.aider.conf.yml.

workspace.reason: Aider loads only files passed with `/read` or `--read`, or listed under `read:` in its configuration.

agents.verify: Start aider and confirm the file is listed as read-only in the session.
agents.local_models: Aider works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including a local model server.
notes: Loading the file with `--read` marks it read-only, so aider will not edit it.
The same file can be listed under `read:` in .aider.conf.yml to load it every session.

sources.quote: It's best to load the conventions file with `/read CONVENTIONS.md` or `aider --read CONVENTIONS.md`.

agents.name: Cline
agents.global_unsupported_reason: Cline global rules are set in its settings UI rather than a user-level file.

workspace.reason: Cline reads project rules from the workspace; an ancestor workspace directory is not documented.

agents.verify: Open the Rules view in the Cline panel and confirm the file is listed.
agents.local_models: Cline supports local model servers through its provider settings.
notes: Rules in .clinerules are picked up automatically by the CLI, VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin.
`~/.clinerules` is the home-directory equivalent for rules that apply to every project.

sources.quote: Define project-specific rules in .clinerules files that guide how Cline works in your codebase. Rules are picked up automatically by the CLI, VS Code extension, and JetBrains plugin.

agents.name: Goose

workspace.reason: Goose reads one global hints file and one project hints file; an ancestor workspace file is not documented.

agents.verify: Ask goose which hints files it loaded for the session.
agents.local_models: Point Goose at a local provider in its configuration.
notes: Global hints apply to all sessions; local hints apply to the project.
When the two conflict, goose prioritizes the local hints.

sources.quote: If the instructions in your local hints file conflict with your global preferences, goose will prioritize the local hints.
